# netactuate_router (Resource)

Beta. The cloud router family is in beta: behaviour and schema may change. Manages a cloud router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netactuate_router" "example" {
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description for your cloud router.
- `location` (String) The location to create the cloud router.
- `location_id` (Number) The id of the location to create the cloud router in.
- `name` (String) Name your cloud router whatever you wish.
- `package_id` (Number) The id of the package for the server which backs your cloud router.
- `plan` (String) Plan/package name for the cloud router (e.g. "VR2x2x25"). Resolved to package_id on create.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `can_join_magic_mesh` (Boolean) Whether the router can join a magic mesh.
- `default_vrf_id` (Number) The ID of the default VRF.
- `has_default_vrf` (Boolean) Whether the router has a default VRF.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ipv4_address` (String) The IPv4 address assigned to the cloud router.
- `mesh_id` (Number) The mesh ID if the router is part of a mesh network.
- `router_id` (Number) The ID of the cloud router.
- `status` (String) The current status of the cloud router (e.g., 'offline', 'active').
- `updated_on` (String) The date when the router was last updated.
- `version` (Number) The configuration version of the router.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import netactuate_router.example 12345
```
